indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for bite from right to left

parts.note: a tang is a sharp bite of flavour

explanation.surface: A tiny insect is about to nip someone in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns TANG (a bite of flavour) into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge-like fly is a classic small insect.

parts.note: profit is gain
a maxim is a saying

explanation.surface: Someone argues against the proverb that profit is everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To gainsay is to deny or contradict, so the participle means contradicting.

parts.note: in the tale of William Tell, the archer shot a fruit placed on his son's head

explanation.surface: A sneak who tells tales is the one everyone aims at.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit balanced on the boy's head was the archer's mark in the legend.

clue.text: The offenders with those who may help them

parts.note: rapists are sexual offenders

explanation.surface: Criminals are paired with counsellors who might reform them.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsellors and psychologists treat people, including criminals, to help them.

clue.text: Not the sole place to find people working at last?

definitions.text: Not the sole place to find people working at last?

parts.words: Not the sole place to find people working at last?
parts.note: read as a shop counter where cobblers work on shoes over a last, mending soles and heels

explanation.surface: Finally, here is somewhere other than the only spot where people are employed.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped block; the shop fixes heels as well as soles, so it is 'not the sole place'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick-repair shoe counter where workers fix footwear on a last.

indicators.note: here the staff stands outside the gallery, wrapping round it

parts.note: a rod is a staff
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: Employees were moved on, out of the art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' is read as 'outside': ROD goes round TATE, the London art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has spun or revolved has been rotated.

clue.text: Charge, in exercises around the border

indicators.note: around says the exercises letters go round the word for border

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: An accusation arises during workouts near the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a gun or pump is to prime it, readying it for use.

indicators.note: new says the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A proclamation from the Christian scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' looks part of 'New Testament' but signals the anagram of TESTAMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement is a formal declaration.

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a sight is a spectacle or exhibition

explanation.surface: Someone has been told where a show will be held.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a place or position.

indicators.note: of in the sense of made out of: the figure is formed from these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A young woman with a trim shape.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of GIRL NEAT are rearranged; 'of' is the weak signal for making the figure out of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided shape is a geometric figure.

explanation.surface: Something faulty and nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: Faulty means flawed; in grammar, the imperfect is a past tense of continuing action.

indicators.note: in places the word for sleep inside the word for thing

parts.note: it can stand for a thing
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: An inappropriate garment to wear to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means inappropriate or ill-fitting.

clue.text: Haggard heroine takes a degree in queenly style

indicators.note: takes says the heroine is followed by the degree

parts.note: She is the title heroine of H. Rider Haggard's novel
BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A gaunt heroine earns a degree in a regal manner.
explanation.walkthrough: Haggard is the novelist H. Rider Haggard, not 'gaunt'; She is his immortal queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Queen of Sheba is the byword for regal splendour.

clue.text: Having made a hole and put article inside, find it's disturbed

indicators.note: inside places the article within the word for made a hole

parts.note: to bore is to drill a hole
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Someone drilled a hole, put something in, and found it upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Bothered means troubled or upset.

clue.text: Plays for time with rate increases

parts.note: tempo is a rate or speed
rises are increases

explanation.surface: Someone stalls as costs go up.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to stall or delay to gain time.

clue.text: What we like to feel we'll never get

definitions.text: What we like to feel we'll never get

parts.words: What we like to feel we'll never get
parts.note: we age every day, so we never grow less old, though we like to feel youthful

explanation.surface: Something we enjoy feeling but will never receive.
explanation.definitionFit: Each day we grow older, so feeling more youthful is something we never actually become.

indicators.note: poorly suggests the letters are badly assembled into another order

explanation.surface: Someone shabbily dressed seems uneducated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like the anagram signal, but its letters are the fodder; 'Poorly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untaught lacks instruction and so is ignorant.

clue.text: Strike out, parking inside, then get run down

indicators.note: inside puts the parking letter within the word for strike out

parts.note: to delete is to strike out
P is the map abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Cross out the line, slip a parking space in, then exhaust supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete is to use up or reduce stocks.

clue.text: They are made to probe cuts requiring surgery

parts.note: a prod is a poke or probe

indicators.note: something requiring surgery must be cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Instruments designed to examine wounds that need an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Products are things manufactured.

clue.text: Breaking stem, gnu gets to the seeds

indicators.note: breaking shatters the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Snapping a stalk, an antelope reaches some seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutmegs are aromatic seeds used as spice.

clue.text: Edible roots about to be wrapped in apron

indicators.note: wrapped in says the word for about sits inside the word for apron

parts.note: an apron is a kind of skirt
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Vegetables about to be bundled up in a pinafore.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirret is a plant grown for its edible roots.

clue.text: Pot of gold turned out to be here

indicators.note: turned out says the letters are turned into a new arrangement

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: The treasure at the rainbow's end proved to be up on the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: POTOF plus OR (heraldic gold) is rearranged; 'here' points to the place the pot turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A housetop is the spot the clue points at, where the treasure was.

parts.note: a professional army soldier, and something uniform is consistent or even

explanation.surface: A trooper wearing battledress.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-time soldier is a professional, and uniform also means even and consistent.

parts.note: a shop holding goods for sale keeps them in stock, and hose is a leg garment

explanation.surface: A shop offers hosiery to customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep goods in stock is to carry them for sale, and a hose is a leg garment.

clue.text: Complaint of the officer in charge

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an officer
IC means in charge

explanation.surface: A grievance made by the commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is an abdominal pain, a medical complaint.

indicators.note: without starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A dinner served with no first course is a cut above.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper means higher in rank or position.

clue.text: In turn, get some tea about teatime

indicators.note: about places the tea letters around the time

parts.note: a pot is some tea
teatime is four o'clock, IV in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Each taking a turn, people get a cuppa round four o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Teatime is traditionally 4pm in Britain, giving the Roman IV.
explanation.definitionFit: To pivot is to swivel or rotate.

indicators.note: back says the assembled letters are read in reverse
hugging puts the word for me inside is

explanation.surface: A rugby player in midfield is holding the speaker tight.
explanation.walkthrough: IS hugging ME gives IMES; 'back' turns it round. A half-back is a sports position.
explanation.definitionFit: Semi is the prefix meaning half.

clue.text: Join up with forsaken sweetheart, rejected

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are turned back

parts.note: lorn means forsaken or forlorn
the heart of sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: Sign up after being jilted by a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to sign up or enlist.

indicators.note: unusually says the letters come in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Words with a common origin are remarkably adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognates are kin by blood, family members.

indicators.note: needs revising says the letters must be reworked

explanation.surface: Evidence that the reference book must be updated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indicatory points out or shows.

parts.note: in the Cole Porter song a young lady regrets she is unable to lunch today

explanation.surface: A young woman skips her midday meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's Miss regrets she cannot lunch, so she is the lady not lunching.
